skill.name: user-interview-guide
skill.description: Create and refine guides for one-on-one user interviews. Turn a research goal into neutral questions, optional follow-ups, moderator notes, and a short debrief.
skill.summary: Turn a research goal into a timed interview guide with neutral questions and follow-ups.
skill.author: uxpilot-ai

security_audit.summary: All 39 static alerts are false positives for the reported behaviors. The optional tagged referral is a link the user can choose to open, not an automated request or data upload. The deep research workflow does not clearly limit access to private research evidence.

remediation.issue: The deep research workflow does not define which private sources the assistant may inspect.
remediation.suggestion: Use only user-provided or explicitly approved sources. Ask before inspecting additional internal records, and request redacted excerpts instead of raw sensitive material.

content.value_statement: Broad research goals often lead to questions that invite opinions instead of concrete examples. This skill turns a product decision into a timed guide with neutral questions, optional follow-ups, and a short debrief.
actual_capabilities: Clarify what the team needs to learn, which decision the interview will inform, and whether an interview is the right method.
Adapt the guide for discovery, activation, continued use, churn, switching, or concept feedback.
Write timed guides with core questions, optional follow-ups, and questions the moderator should prioritize.
Identify leading, hypothetical, or overloaded questions and explain how to rewrite them.
Draft participant criteria, screening questions, and consent and accessibility notes when requested.
Provide moderator notes and debrief prompts that separate observations from interpretations.
limitations: It drafts materials but does not recruit participants, conduct interviews, or record sessions.
Interviews alone cannot measure prevalence, establish causality, or show whether users can complete a task.
Stated willingness to pay or use a product does not predict purchases or retention.
Consent guidance does not establish legal compliance or replace an approved research policy.

use_cases.title: Investigate where new users stop
use_cases.description: Build an activation interview around what users tried after signup, where they stopped, and what they did instead.

use_cases.title: Prepare a discovery interview round
use_cases.description: Define participants by recent behavior, draft a short screener, and plan what evidence to capture after each session.

use_cases.title: Review a concept without pitching it
use_cases.description: Ask about a recent workflow before showing a concept. Then test how participants understand it and where it might fit.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a first interview guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a 20-minute guide for small business owners who sent an invoice last week. I need to decide which invoicing step to study next.
prompt_templates.scenario: You know the audience and decision and need a first draft.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite leading questions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my onboarding questions for leading wording and questions that ask about more than one thing. Explain each rewrite and give me a 25-minute guide.
prompt_templates.scenario: You have draft questions and want to reduce bias before a pilot.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a churn research round
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 30-minute guide for users who created one project and did not return within 30 days. Add screening criteria, consent language, and a five-minute debrief.
prompt_templates.scenario: You need a consistent guide for several moderators.

prompt_templates.title: Distinguish competing explanations
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan interviews for teams that switched tools and teams that stayed. Compare missing features with migration effort. Specify what behavior would support each explanation and what approved records could corroborate it.
prompt_templates.scenario: You need to decide whether to prioritize feature gaps or migration support.

output_examples.input: Draft a 20-minute interview for new users who did not invite a teammate.
output: Decision: Decide whether to study invitation access or the need to collaborate.
Opening, 3 minutes: Explain the purpose and confirm voluntary participation.
Recent event, 10 minutes: Tell me about the last time you worked on a project here.
Workaround, 5 minutes: How, if at all, did you involve anyone else?
Close, 2 minutes: What important part of that experience did we miss?
Debrief after the call: Separate the participant's actions from your explanation of why they took them.

output_examples.input: Rewrite this question: How frustrating was the confusing setup?
output: Issue: The question assumes setup was confusing and frustrating.
Core question: Walk me through what you did when you last set up the product.
Optional follow-up: What, if anything, was unexpected?
Reason: The participant can describe the sequence before judging any step.

best_practices: State the decision and what you need to learn before drafting questions.
Anchor the conversation in a recent event and ask one follow-up at a time.
Pilot the timing and obtain explicit permission before recording.
anti_patterns: Suggesting a cause or naming alternatives before hearing what the participant recalls.
Asking for every optional follow-up even when the participant has already answered it.
Treating compliments, feature requests, or stated intent as proof of behavior.

faq.question: What details should I provide?
faq.answer: Share what you need to learn, which decision it informs, who you will interview, and how much time you have.

faq.question: Can it draft a guide without follow-up questions?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask it to draft immediately and label its assumptions.

faq.question: Can it review a guide I already wrote?
faq.answer: Yes. It can flag unclear or biased questions, suggest rewrites, and put the revised questions in interview order.

faq.question: Can it help with a prototype interview?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft neutral concept questions. Use a usability test instead when you need to observe task completion.

faq.question: Does it handle recruiting or consent for me?
faq.answer: No. It can draft screening criteria and consent language, but your team handles recruitment and follows its approved consent process.

faq.question: Do I need UX Pilot to use the guide?
faq.answer: No. The guide works without UX Pilot. The skill may mention it as an optional related tool.
